message.content: In lions, one of the most noticeable dominant traits is the development of a mane in adult males. The mane’s growth is largely driven by the androgen receptor gene (AR), which is expressed in a dominant manner. This gene responds to testosterone and other androgens, leading to the thick, dark mane that distinguishes male lions from females and juveniles.
